summary: The paper proposes DIRECTER, an inference-time activation-steering method that mitigates oversteering by (a) KV-cache key scaling, (b) a plausibility-guided decoding loop that progressively reduces the number of steered layers when the steered top token is implausible under the raw distribution, and (c) a one-time attention-sensitivity layer ranking. Evaluation is fairly comprehensive across IFEval, LIFBench, a self-designed GSM8K-Format, multiple model families/scales, ablations, efficiency, and LLM/human quality judging, and DIRECTER consistently (if modestly) beats tuned steering baselines without per-task tuning. The core weaknesses are moderate novelty (a recombination of contrastive/plausibility decoding, KV steering, and sensitivity ranking), modest absolute gains, and the absence of significance testing on the main comparisons.
strengths: Addresses a real and well-motivated problem (oversteering) with a mechanism that is dynamic and self-correcting rather than a fixed hyperparameter, and shows the plausibility filter transfers to PASTA/SpotLight as a general safety gate (Figure 2b).

Strong robustness/generality evidence: fixed hyperparameters (alpha=100, beta=0.5) applied across all tasks, gains across Llama-3.2-1B through Qwen-2.5-14B (Table 2), and stability across beta and several orders of magnitude of alpha (Figure 3).

Careful attention to the trade-off DIRECTER claims to avoid: it reports task fidelity and text quality via LLM judge (Table 4) plus corroborating human evaluation, and analyzes efficiency (throughput, per-token latency, memory, FlashAttention compatibility).
Ablations isolate the key design choices (ranking reversed, random layers, random tokens, fixed-strength ST_k), supporting the claim that principled layer selection and dynamic strength both matter.

key_concerns.issue: No statistical significance testing on the main results. Greedy decoding makes single runs deterministic, but the ~2-4 point gaps over tuned baselines on benchmarks of finite size (e.g., IFEval) are not tested for significance (e.g., McNemar / bootstrap over items), so it is unclear the improvements are real rather than noise.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add item-level paired significance tests (or bootstrap CIs) over benchmark instances for the main comparisons in Table 1, and report variance where any stochasticity exists.

key_concerns.issue: Several load-bearing justifications are deferred to appendices not evaluable here: why modulate L rather than alpha (App C.4), key vs value scaling (App C.5), the disturbance-score formulation (App C), and span-detection robustness (App D.2). The main text asserts these conclusions without in-body evidence, and the sensitivity metric (Eq. 2) is acknowledged as heuristic with no theoretical grounding.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Bring the core empirical justifications (key-vs-value, L-vs-alpha, and at least a summary of the sensitivity-metric ablation) into the main body, and motivate the disturbance score more rigorously.

key_concerns.issue: Novelty is incremental: plausibility/contrastive decoding (Li et al. 2022; Chuang et al. 2023) and KV/attention steering are pre-existing; the contribution is their combination plus dynamic layer-count reduction. The absolute gains over the best tuned baseline (~4 points average) are modest.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Sharpen the delineation from contrastive decoding and articulate what is fundamentally new beyond applying an accept/reject test to steering; consider a stronger head-to-head against a contrastive-decoding baseline.

key_concerns.issue: GSM8K-Format is a self-designed benchmark, raising a risk of favorable construction; DIRECTER is not strictly best on every sub-metric (e.g., GSM8K T.Acc 86.9 vs Few-shot 87.1).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report construction details and, ideally, an independently designed formatting benchmark, and temper any implied dominance to 'best on average'.

key_concerns.issue: alpha=100 (and stability up to 1e5) key scaling is unusual and effectively saturates attention onto instruction tokens; the paper leans on this to argue L (not alpha) is the useful control knob, but the mechanism deserves clearer in-text explanation.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Explain in the body why extreme key scaling is benign after softmax renormalization and why layer-count is the more graduated control.

questions_for_authors: Are the Table 1/2 improvements statistically significant at the item level, and what test/effect size supports the ~4-point gap over tuned SpotLight/PASTA?
How sensitive are results to the gpt-4o-mini prompt rewriting of IFEval and to using gpt-4o-mini as the quality/fidelity judge (any bias favoring your outputs)?
What is the failure mode when no steered distribution passes the plausibility filter across all layer subsets, and how often does the loop fall back to the raw distribution?
Can you quantify how frequently the gating mechanism skips steering, and confirm it never changes outputs relative to the full loop as claimed?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly well scoped ('up to 6.5%', 'approximately 4%', explicit limitations and robustness ranges), though 'general mechanism' and 'model-agnostic' are somewhat strong given the modest gains and lack of significance testing.

significance.justification: A practical, drop-in improvement to activation steering that also transfers to other methods; useful to the subfield but not paradigm-shifting given modest gains.

novelty.justification: Primarily a novel combination of contrastive/plausibility decoding, KV-cache steering, and a sensitivity-based layer ranking; the dynamic layer-count reduction is the main new element.

rigor.justification: Method is sound and ablations isolate components, but key justifications are deferred to appendices and the sensitivity metric is admittedly heuristic.

statistical_soundness.justification: Main comparisons lack significance testing or CIs; greedy decoding mitigates run variance but does not address whether small benchmark gaps are meaningful, though some ablations do report std.

calibration_honesty.justification: Gains are hedged, limitations and robustness ranges are reported, and negative/failure behaviors are discussed rather than hidden.

clarity.justification: The method and RQ-driven experiments are reasonably clear, but heavy appendix reliance and dense notation reduce standalone readability of the main text.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard conference structure with Abstract, Intro, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Conclusion, and appropriate length.

reproducibility.justification: Named models, fixed hyperparameters, and greedy decoding are specified, but several procedural details (span detection, metric simplification, tuning) live only in appendices.

related_work.justification: Instruction-following and activation-steering lines are covered and DIRECTER is positioned against PASTA and SpotLight, though differentiation from contrastive-decoding methods is thin.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative, claim-supporting comparisons (fixed-strength ablation, compatibility, robustness sweeps, efficiency), adequate to judge the corresponding claims.

breadth_generality.justification: Multiple benchmarks, model families and scales, and several ablations support generality, but 'general mechanism' claims outrun the modest, untested gains.

overall_recommendation.justification: A sound, competently evaluated but incremental steering method with modest gains; borderline accept pending significance testing and stronger in-body justification.
